# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 16
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "brightness of the light which was in him" vs. "brightness of the light in him"
- **EMET:** "brightness of the light which was in him did not cease"
- **LOGOS:** "brightness of the light in him did not cease"
- **PNEUMA:** "brightness in him never stopped. It kept radiating, ceaselessly"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "kept radiating, ceaselessly" repeats the concept twice. LOGOS's compression is preferable.

### v.2 — "They shone with brightness ten times greater"
- All agents agree on the numeral. PNEUMA adds "blazing with" — minor.

### v.2 — "Their whiteness was more white than any snow" vs. "whiter than any snow"
- **EMET:** "their whiteness was more white than any snow"
- **LOGOS:** "their whiteness was whiter than any snow"
- **PNEUMA:** "their whiteness was beyond any snow"
- **Note:** "Beyond any snow" (PNEUMA) is a paraphrase; "whiter than any snow" (LOGOS) is more precise.

### v.3 — "they greatly praised the Lord, they and all the angels"
- **EMET:** "they greatly praised the Lord, they and all the angels who praised him together"
- **LOGOS:** "they praised the Lord greatly, together with all the angels who praised him"
- **PNEUMA:** "they and all the angels together, voices filling everything"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "voices filling everything" is an addition.

### v.4 — "What will be the end of this vision?"
- All agents agree. PNEUMA's "What do you think this vision means? What will become of it?" unpacks into two questions not in source.

### v.5 — "our understanding was taken from us"
- All agents agree on this striking phrase. PNEUMA's "before we could even form a thought" is an expansion.

### v.6 — "in the manner of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob" vs. "in the way of"
- Minor. All agents agree on substance.

### v.6 — "crown of faith"
- All agents agree. No disagreement.

### v.7 — "speak two words" — all agents agree on "two words" idiomatic reading.

### v.8 — "Speak what you wish, my Lord"
- All agents preserve the remarkable phrase "my Lord" addressed by Christ to Peter. No one softens it.

### v.10 — "He smiled at me" (PNEUMA only)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** Not present.
- **PNEUMA:** Adds "He smiled at me" before the Lord's words.
- **Note:** Not in source. A narrative intrusion, however emotionally appealing. Rejected by SOPHIA.

### v.10 — "You see the kingdom of heaven in advance" vs. "you are looking at the kingdom before it has come"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "You see the kingdom of heaven in advance"
- **PNEUMA:** "you are looking at the kingdom of heaven before it has come"
- **Note:** Equivalent in meaning. EMET/LOGOS's "in advance" is the more concise rendering.

---
*11 disagreements. SOPHIA: reject "He smiled at me" (v.10); "whiter than any snow" (v.2); "brightness... in him did not cease" (v.1).*
